subject: Request: onboard 'Orchid-13B' variant and pin for Acme pilot
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, orchid-support@orchid.ai
Date: Sat, 14 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: onboard 'Orchid-13B' variant and pin for Acme pilot

Hi team,

Acme Health (Jake Hollis) verbally committed to a month-long pilot starting 2026-03-23 that requires us to serve Orchid-13B with a pinned variant. They want predictable inference behavior while they evaluate accuracy vs their prompts. Two asks:

1) Can infra onboard the Orchid-13B model (orchid-13b-v1.2.0) and expose a pinned serving variant (orchid-13b-v1.2.0-8bit) in our hosted catalog for the Acme pilot? They specifically asked that the variant not receive automatic rolling updates during the pilot (pin for the duration).

2) Product needs an infra compatibility/behavior check document: memory footprint, expected latency at 1-4 concurrent requests per user session, quantization tolerances, and recommended KV-cache settings for 4096 max-seq.

Background: Acme expects ~120 concurrent users during peak hours, average 350 tokens/session, latency SLO <= 450ms p95 for single-turn prompts. They will stream responses. Budget for the pilot is capped, so we should estimate token-unit cost impact of this variant.

Attachments: orchid-13b-ckpt-manifest.txt (model manifest Orchid provided) and acme-pilot-mop.xlsx (expected usage matrix from the AE).

Timeline: they want a staging endpoint and pinned variant available by 2026-03-20 so they can run their evals. If pinning requires an exception to our normal rollout rules, please flag it.

Action requested: Dev, can you confirm feasibility and list follow-ups? Laura, can you confirm product acceptance criteria for the pilot? Vivek, please confirm any compliance gating.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, orchid-support@orchid.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: onboard 'Orchid-13B' variant and pin for Acme pilot

Thanks Marissa — quick read and a few technical clarifications before I kick off the onboarding work. I've created a short JIRA INF-6723 to track the infra tasks.

Questions / notes:
- Model artifact: the manifest references a 13B FP16 checkpoint and a separate 8-bit quant bundle. Do we have the actual quantized artifact or should we run quantization on our side? If we run quantization, please confirm the target bits (8-bit, 4-bit, or GPTQ) and tolerances.
- KV cache: for 4096 max-seq we need to know expected per-request cache retention/expires. Do we expect many multi-turn sessions or single-turn streaming? That affects memory and batching.
- Batching policy: at the projected 120 concurrent users, what's the average QPS? If it's spiky, we'll need to set burst capacity in Dedicated or use our hosted burst lanes.
- Licensing: orchid's manifest has a non-standard commercial clause (section 4.2). Legal needs to confirm we can serve the model in hosted mode; otherwise, private or dedicated might be required.

What I can do immediately:
- Run a compatibility sanity run on a 32GB GPU with the provided FP16 checkpoint and estimate memory and latency numbers (need the artifact).
- If you want us to produce a quantized variant, we can run GPTQ, but that will add ~2 business days and requires a test prompt set from Acme to validate quality drop.
- I can pin a model variant in our catalog, but pinning a new variant across hosted fleets requires a temporary rollout exception (we normally tie variants to auto-updates). Ops can grant a one-off exception for the pilot window; I'll note that in INF-6723.

Please attach the actual model artifacts (or a secure link) and a 10–20 prompt sample set for quality checks.

-- Dev
Senior Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: onboard 'Orchid-13B' variant and pin for Acme pilot

Looping in compliance concerns while we evaluate. High-level items:

- License review: if Orchid's manifest has a restrictive commercial clause we cannot proceed in hosted mode without legal sign-off. Marissa, please share the vendor contract / license text.
- Data retention: for a pilot we should limit request/response retention to 7 days for this tenant and block model telemetry export unless Acme explicitly opts-in. Ops/infra will need a per-tenant retention override.
- SOC2 / attestation: Acme asked for confirmation around SOC2 controls for model artifacts and access. Our standard SOC2 scope covers hosted infra but not third-party model handling; we will need to log access to the model blob and restrict admin access.

If infra expects to pin a variant, we should document the exception and duration (start/end dates). Also confirm whether pinning prevents rollback in our automated fallback system — we should still allow emergency fallback to a smaller model for availability.

I'll ask Legal and InfoSec to prioritize review but they will need the artifact manifest and vendor contact (orchid-support@orchid.ai) included in the packet.

Vivek
VP Sales & Compliance | Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: onboard 'Orchid-13B' variant and pin for Acme pilot

Thanks all — summary and owners so we can hit the 2026-03-20 staging target: 

Decisions/Plan:
- Infra (Dev) to run compatibility/runbook: dev will attempt a sanity run on 3/17 and provide memory/latency estimates and a recommended quantization path (either use Orchid-provided 8-bit or run GPTQ internally). Deliverable: "Orchid compatibility matrix" (attachment orchid-13b-compat-matrix.csv).
- Legal & InfoSec (Vivek to coordinate) to review license and SOC2 impacts by 3/18. Deliverable: legal sign-off email + retention override ticket.
- Product (Laura) will provide acceptance criteria for pilot by EOD 3/17: expected p95 latency <= 450ms, quality delta < 3% on the provided prompt set, streaming support validated.
- Sales (Marissa) will supply the 20-sample prompt set and the vendor contact link (orchid-support@orchid.ai).
- Ops: temporary rollout exception documented in INF-6723; pin will be set from 2026-03-20 to 2026-04-20, after which auto-updates resume unless extension requested. Emergency fallback policy: allow fallback to "redwood-gpt-medium" with explicit manual approval.

If everyone can ack here, I will convert this into an internal doc and attach the acceptance criteria and rollout checklist. We will keep the staging endpoint internal to Acme and Orchids until sign-off.

Laura
Product Manager | Redwood Inference
